report:
I can see an interpretable bias, though I can’t pin a specific training objective beyond a domain/style shift.

What stands out
- The difference is overwhelmingly concentrated at the first token (p0) across mid–late layers, with substantial spillover to early positions (p1–p4). That points to a start-of-sequence style/genre prior.
- Logit-lens top tokens repeatedly cluster around:
  - News/headline lexicon and proper nouns: headline(s), Driver, van/von, President, Royals, Manny, Vincent, Hunter, Segundo, Raipur, Malawi, UFO, podcast.
  - Sensational/pop-media adjectives: iconic, tragic, tragedy, vivid, colorful, lush, vibrant, loud, melodic, timeless, furry; also victims, refugees, hurricane, moments, names, reactions.
  - Some assistant-ish/instruction tokens appear (consider, recommend, relevant, optimize, prevent, check), but they’re less consistent than the “news/pop-media” cluster.

Interpretation
- Model B appears more primed toward news/arts-entertainment/pop-culture style, especially headline-like openings and listicle/review adjectives (“iconic/tragic/vivid/timeless”) and named entities common in news/sports/entertainment.
- This manifests strongest at the beginning of the sequence (consistent with a headline/lede prior), and persists through later layers.

Conclusion
- Likely difference: a domain/style shift making Model B more “newsy/pop-media” in its lexical prior at the start of text. I cannot identify a more specific objective (e.g., RLHF for safety or a particular task) from this evidence alone.
